narrative.overview:
Quranku is a sheet of paper on a desk. Each theme is a paper (White, Cream, Green, Night, or one the reader mixes), with one ink for text, one muted ink for everything secondary, and one accent. Nothing is drawn on the paper for its own sake: the Quran text, its ayah marks and its surah titles are the only ornament, and the chrome around them is flat, thin-lined and quiet. The app opens on today's reading (the verse where the reader stopped, in Arabic, at reading size) and reading itself is a full-window view entered with Continue and left with Esc.

Density is relaxed. Pages are centered columns with generous outer margins (36 top, 40 sides, 48 bottom) and a 28px rhythm between blocks; lists are airy rows that only show a fill on hover. Depth comes from stepping between the paper's tones (Page, Surface, Desk) and from 1px hairlines, not from shadows. Tajweed help, translation and recitation sit in the same quiet register as the chrome so they never compete with the text.

This is a native desktop UI drawn by MyGo in Go. There is no CSS: every value below lives in Go code (`themes.go`, `tajweed.go`, and the views). The theme radius is 8.
keyCharacteristics: Paper themes with a fixed role set: Page, Desk, Surface, Hover, Border, Text, Muted, Accent.
One accent per paper, spent on the primary action, progress, the current selection and the text's own ornaments.
Emphasis by fading what surrounds, never by drawing boxes.
One platform sans for the UI; Amiri Quran (or Scheherazade New) for Arabic.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no gradients.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each paper has one accent. It marks the primary action (Continue, Begin, Next, the player's play button), progress (goal bars, the reader's edge line, juz progress, the 14-day chart), and current selection (nav item, picked surah, picked reciter, picked theme, selected choice card). The only other place it appears is the text's own ornament: ayah marks, surah titles in Arabic, the Mushaf frame and surah header lozenge. Selection is shown as an accent wash at 0.12-0.14 alpha with accent bold label text, never a solid accent block.

rules.name: The Accent Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on a solid accent is white (`accent-text-light`) unless the accent's luminance exceeds 0.6, then near-black (`accent-text-dark`). Auto's dark appearance uses `auto-dark-accent-text`.

rules.name: The Four Colors Rule
rules.body: A custom theme is four chosen colors (Page, Surface, Text, Accent); the rest are mixed, never chosen: Desk is Surface mixed 8% toward Text, Hover 7%, Border 14%, Muted is Text mixed 42% toward Page. A theme is dark when its Page luminance is under 0.5.

rules.name: The One Sans Rule
rules.body: The UI uses the platform sans alone. Do not introduce a display face; weight and size carry the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Core Text Rule
rules.body: Arabic is set only in Amiri Quran or Scheherazade New. Faces whose marks Core Text drops (KFGQPC, Digital Khatt) are not used.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Numbers that line up or tick (verse keys, surah numbers, page counts, slider values, stats) use `tnum`.

rules.name: The Centered Column Rule
rules.body: Section content sits in a centered column with a maximum width: Home, Stats and wide Settings 1280; Settings 780 when the content area is under 1100; Shuffle 960; onboarding 720; verse-by-verse reading 880 (with 32px side padding). The column has 36 / 40 / 48 outer padding and a 28px gap between blocks.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat paper with hairline edges. Separate by tone and line, not by lift; no gradients, no glass, no colored shadows.

rules.name: The Edge Progress Rule
rules.body: Today's goal progress runs as a 3px, square-ended line along the reader bar's bottom edge. The reader shows progress there and in the bar's subtitle, nowhere else.

rules.name: The Esc Rule
rules.body: Esc leaves the reader for Home; the back button says so in its label. In the Mushaf, the left arrow and Page Down go to the next page (right to left, as the book reads).

rules.name: The Fading Emphasis Rule
rules.body: Tajweed is taught by fading the surroundings, never by boxes, outlines or backgrounds behind letters. Hovering a colored letter keeps it at full color and fades the rest of that verse (or Mushaf page) to 0.3 alpha. While a verse plays on a Mushaf page, the other verses rest at 0.38. When the guide focuses one rule, other rules' letters lose their color and return to Text. The hover tooltip is the rule card: Page background, hairline, radius 10, 280 wide, a rule-color dot, name, Arabic name in the rule color, and a one-line summary.

dos: Do take every color from the current paper's roles (Page, Desk, Surface, Hover, Border, Text, Muted, Accent) so all five built-in papers and every custom theme work unchanged.
Do keep the accent to the primary action, progress, current selection and the text's ornaments (ayah marks, surah titles, Mushaf frame).
Do show selection as an accent wash (0.12-0.14) with accent bold text.
Do emphasize a tajweed rule by fading its surroundings (0.3 on hover, 0.38 for quiet verses).
Do center section content in a column capped at its width (1280, 960, 880, 720) with 36 / 40 / 48 padding and a 28 gap.
Do name every icon-only button and give it a tooltip.
Do use tabular figures for numbers that align or change.
donts: Don't put boxes, outlines or backgrounds around tajweed letters.
Don't use gradients, glass, or heavy and colored shadows; the three soft ambient shadows (Mushaf page, continue panel, rule card) are the whole vocabulary.
Don't add a second UI typeface or set the UI in a display face.
Don't set Arabic in fonts Core Text cannot mark correctly.
Don't spend the accent on headings, decoration or large fills.
Don't add chrome to the reader beyond back, surah, play, mode and Aa; tajweed and guide switches live in the Aa menu.
